title: Arp SHUF, RAND and TM, the Turing Machine loop (base 0.2)
author: naturarum
description: EXPERIMENT: emulator-tested only. The arpeggiator's SHUF and RAND, which the Digitone II names but plays as CYCL: SHUF plays every held note in every octave of RANGE once per cycle, in a new random order each cycle; RAND a random held note in a random octave of RANGE at each step. The steps' on/off and offsets, LEN, SPEED and N.LEN work as in the stock modes. 0.2: TM, a Turing Machine loop after the eighth MODE: a 16-bit shift register per track moves at every step of the arp, its bit leaving the loop (ARP LENGTH steps) coming back in flipped with the chance LOOP CHANGE / 100 (knob E in TM: 0 locks the loop, 50 every step new, 100 the loop inverted every other time); the note is its low 8 bits scaled over the held notes and the octaves of RANGE; the step graph shows the loop's notes live; the steps' offsets are not added in TM. TM is MODE 7..107 (LOOP CHANGE in the MODE byte), so kits keep their format. A kit saved with SHUF, RAND or TM opens on a stock OS with its arp OFF. Inspired by research findings of dn2_firmware_explore (angellinares) on OS 1.11; TM after Tom Whitwell's Turing Machine; this is our own code. For dn2-cfw's base 0.2.
